title: Hidden Sugar
subtitle: Free sugars hide behind many names.
description: An ingredient does not need to be called 'sugar' to act like sugar in your body. BOTIA reads the label and flags what it finds — classified according to WHO free sugar categories.
why_body: Products labelled 'natural', 'fit' or 'healthy' often use ingredients that behave like sugar while avoiding the word. WHO recommends keeping free sugar intake below 10% of total daily energy — ideally below 5%.
what_body: BOTIA detects ingredients classified as free sugars by WHO criteria, organised into four categories.
cat1_desc: Glucose, fructose, sucrose, dextrose — the most common added sugars.
cat2_desc: Glucose syrup, corn syrup, high fructose corn syrup — liquid concentrated sugars.
cat3_desc: Maltodextrin, dextrin, hydrolyzed starch — technically not sugar, processed the same way.
cat4_desc: Concentrated fruit juice used as sweetener — classified as free sugar by WHO.
can_1: Detect ingredients classified as free sugars by WHO criteria.
can_2: Categorise them into the correct WHO free sugar group.
can_3: Signal when a product marketed as healthy contains these ingredients.
cannot_1: Tell you the total sugar content — check the nutrition label.
cannot_2: Determine whether this product suits your diet.
closing: To assess total intake, check the nutrition label under 'Carbohydrates — of which sugars'.
source_note: WHO Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children (2015) · EFSA Scientific Opinion on dietary sugars (2022)
